main_body: A wooden pew bench drawn straight from the front: horizontal brown planks (backrest slats and seat bands) between two vertical side posts, with no seat surface seen from above.
top_band: none; rows 0-2 are dark brown, then mid-brown slats. The lighter orange bands at rows 7-9 and 10-11 are a seat or rail seen face-on, not a distinct top surface above a front face.
evidence: In the middle column, rows 0-2 are dark brown and rows 3-5 mid-brown with dark stripes. Rows 7-9 are an orange band, 10-11 orange again, and 12-14 dark brown. These are alternating horizontal slat bands with no foreshortened lighter top, no front-edge line, and no eave shadow. The seat of the pew is not seen from above, so it is a front elevation of a bench.

style.evidence: The candidate is a plain wooden bench made of horizontal plank bands in a few brown tones. The outline is a dark brown tint, which is acceptable. The planks are flat fills with only faint grain dots on the light band. It has far fewer shading steps and less tile detail than the stall and well references, which carry per-tile highlights, grain and stone texture. It reads thinner and flatter next to them.
